finding.claim: Broken authorization: update_doc calls can_edit() but discards the boolean result instead of calling require_edit(), so any authenticated user can overwrite any document's body regardless of ownership or editor membership. The sibling update_title route correctly uses require_edit.
finding.source: Any authenticated user (g.user) sending PUT /doc/<doc_id> with JSON {"body": ...} for a doc_id they do not own or edit
finding.sink: doc["body"] = request.json["body"] (docs.py:20) — write to the document body

trace.note: doc = DOCS[doc_id] fetched without any ownership check
can_edit(g.user, doc) result ignored — no abort(403)

finding.guards_checked: can_edit is called but its return value is unused; require_edit (which aborts 403) is not used on this route. No before_request/auth decorator in the file; g.user is assumed set elsewhere (not present in this directory), which authenticates but does not authorize per-document.

verdict.guard_found: can_edit() at docs.py:7-8 returns a bool, but its result is discarded at docs.py:19. require_edit() at docs.py:11-13 aborts 403 but is only used on the title route (docs.py:27). There is no decorator or before_request hook.
verdict.reason: docs.py:19 calls can_edit(g.user, doc) as a bare statement, so the boolean is never tested. docs.py:20 then writes the body for any caller, while the title route at docs.py:27 correctly uses require_edit. Any authenticated low-privilege user can overwrite any document's body. Where g.user is set is outside this directory, but that does not change the missing per-document check.

verdict_facts.guard_found: none effective: can_edit (docs.py:7) returns a bool, but its result is discarded at docs.py:19. require_edit (docs.py:11), which aborts 403, is not called on this route. No decorator or before_request check exists.
verdict_facts.reason: docs.py:19 calls can_edit(g.user, doc) as a bare statement and never aborts, so docs.py:20 overwrites the body for any authenticated user. update_title at docs.py:27 correctly uses require_edit.
